finding.claim: The /checkout endpoint computes the charge from client-supplied price and qty. An attacker can set price to a tiny value, or qty or price to negative numbers, to pay little or nothing or to produce a negative charge (a refund or credit). The sibling /checkout-v2 shows the intended design: it looks up price server-side and clamps qty to an integer of at least 1.
finding.source: req.body.items[].price and req.body.items[].qty, sent by any authenticated client in the POST /checkout JSON body
finding.sink: req.payments.charge(req.user.id, total) at cart.js:6, which charges the attacker-controlled total

trace.note: total = sum of i.price * i.qty, taken directly from the request body with no catalog lookup, type check or range check
The unvalidated total is passed to the payment charge
The attacker-controlled total is echoed back as the charged amount

finding.guards_checked: There is no price lookup, no validation that qty is a positive integer, no check that total is greater than 0, and no check that items is an array. The v2 route's server-side catalog price and Math.max(1, Math.floor(qty)) are absent here. No router-level middleware is visible in this file. cart.js is the only file in the repository, so I could not check for guards elsewhere, such as upstream validation or authentication middleware.

verdict.reason: cart.js:5 sums client-supplied i.price * i.qty with no catalog lookup or range check, and cart.js:6 charges that total, unlike /checkout-v2 at cart.js:13-14. Any logged-in user can reach it. cart.js is the only file, so upstream middleware could not be checked, but nothing in it would validate item prices.
